items.stem: Which explanation best connects a stateless LLM to the need for an agent harness?

options.text: The harness supplies context, tools, memory, state, execution, and feedback around the model.
The LLM stores every conversation internally once it is fine-tuned.
Memory removes the need for a context window.
The harness is only a user-interface layer.

items.stem: A user’s preferred output style is an example of which long-term memory type?

options.text: Procedural memory: knowing how.
Semantic memory: knowing that.
Episodic memory: remembering when.
Short-term working memory only.

items.stem: Which statements correctly distinguish short-term and long-term memory? Select all that apply.

options.text: Short-term memory helps keep the current run coherent.
Long-term memory can carry useful context across sessions and time.
Long-term memory is only the previous turn in a chat.
Procedural, semantic, and episodic are long-term categories in the PowerUP model.

items.stem: What is the main point of Glean’s two signal streams for writing memory?

options.text: Glean learns from assistant traces and enterprise activity, then consolidates those signals into longer-lived memory.
Glean learns only when a user explicitly types a memory command in chat.
Enterprise activity replaces assistant traces entirely.
The model writes directly to a customer database without a consolidation path.

items.stem: Why does the PowerUP describe progressive disclosure for memory retrieval?

options.text: To load a compact summary and selectively retrieve relevant slices instead of injecting the whole archive.
To hide all memory from the model until the user asks for it.
To guarantee that every memory is loaded on every turn.
To replace enterprise search with a single profile file.

items.stem: A customer asks whether a newly learned memory will appear immediately across every AI surface. What is the best response?

options.text: Confirm daily consolidation may delay appearance, and verify deployment and surface availability before promising cross-surface behavior.
Yes. All memory is immediate and identical everywhere.
No. Memory is locked to the original chat surface.
Yes, but users cannot view or delete it.
